s1.syndrome_frame: a gradually enlarging cutaneous tumor with a hard nodule
salient_findings: red tumor on the right upper arm
key_facts: 16-year-old girl
previously healthy
tumor enlarged over 6 months
no history of local trauma or insect bite
personal, past, and family histories were unremarkable
6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red tumor
nontender, firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor
normal laboratory tests
normal physical and systemic examinations
multilocular spaces below the epidermis
solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface
basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis
dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor

raw.rationale: The presence of basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis, along with the description of a solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface, is characteristic of Pilomatrixoma.

rejected.label: Trichoepithelioma
rejected.why: Trichoepithelioma typically presents with multiple small lesions and is often associated with a familial syndrome, which does not match the solitary and sporadic nature of the case.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Basal cell carcinoma is rare in teenagers and typically presents with a history of sun exposure or other risk factors, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is a rare tumor that typically presents with a history of local trauma and has a more aggressive clinical course, which does not match the case.

rejected.label: Cylindroma
rejected.why: Cylindroma is a rare tumor that typically presents with multiple lesions and is often associated with a familial syndrome, which does not match the solitary and sporadic nature of the case.
